source.title: Towards Identification and Intervention of Safety-Critical Parameters in Large Language Models
source.authors: Wei-Wei Qi; Ze-Feng Wu; Tian-Hang Zheng; Zikang Zhang; Xiao-Jun Jia; Zhan Qin; Kui Ren

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: Tests effects of benign downstream fine-tuning on harmful-request ASR and tests parameter localization by perturbing ESI-ranked weights, using methods different from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The study measures harmful-request ASR after downstream task fine-tuning and after parameter perturbation. SET fine-tunes unaligned base models on safe refusal data to induce safety, so those results are not evidence about harmful fine-tuning eroding existing safety. Layer distributions and ESI scores are used for identification; they are not separate behavioral outcomes for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Benign downstream fine-tuning (AGNews, MedicalQA, GSM8K) of instruction-tuned models is measured for harmful-request ASR, which bears on V2. Perturbing ESI-ranked weight subsets versus random subsets is measured for ASR, which bears on V5. Both use methods that differ from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ESI finds safety-critical parameters better than prior metrics, and that these sit in middle-layer value matrices in dense models and late-layer MLP experts in MoE models. SET aligns under-aligned models by updating about 1% of weights. SPA keeps safety degradation within about 1–2% during downstream fine-tuning with no utility cost.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a 10% selective parameter-update budget for downstream task adaptation and perturbs ESI-ranked weights for localization; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-position analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported safety degradation during adaptation differs substantially between Random or RSN-Tune parameter selection and SPA; SPA results are reported separately across models, tasks, and safety benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: SET updates only the top 1% of ESI weights of base (unaligned) models on refusal data for 100 iterations. This cuts ASR by 33–65 points, within about 1–2 points of full fine-tuning (Tables 2, 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety behaviour can be installed by training a small, specifically chosen parameter subset.

fits_no_version.finding: ESI mass is concentrated in middle-layer value matrices for dense models and in late-layer MLP experts for MoE models (Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of safety-critical parameters differs by architecture.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The fine-tuning safety results use a fixed 10% update budget and specific downstream tasks; the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these table values. The localization results are based on perturbation and ASR, not direct measurement of the causal mechanism in ordinary fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: To remain within the 60-row limit, omitted the other perturbation ratios and methods in Table 1, as well as the additional models and perturbation conditions in Appendix Table 5. The retained rows include ESI at 1%, a random control for Llama3-8B-it on both benchmarks, and ESI results for additional architectures.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning of aligned models on harmful examples.

Only 10%-parameter-budget selective fine-tuning on three task datasets was tested. Not tested: full-parameter or LoRA benign fine-tuning, identity-shifting or carefully chosen benign data, and few-example regimes.
No per-token KL or token-position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks; WildJailbreak prompts are used only as an evaluation set.
Localization was tested only by Gaussian-noise perturbation of individual weights ranked by ESI. Not tested: low-rank localization, and whether perturbation also damages general capability.
No test of why safety is shallow.
No training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens. SPA and SET are parameter-selection methods.

missing.what: ESI 1% WildJailbreak results for Llama3-70B-it (34.2→65.2) and Qwen3-30B-A3B-it (30.3→50.6), with their random controls
ESI perturbation on Qwen2.5-14B-it, Qwen2.5-72B-it, Mixtral-8x7B-it and Qwen3-235B-A22B-it (e.g. HB 1%: 13→37.1, 19.5→45.9, 20.1→66.8, 9.1→33.1), with random controls
Comparison with the SN/GMT/Wanda/SNIP selection metrics, which show smaller effects at the same budget
0.1% ESI perturbation, which already gives large rises (Llama3-8B HB 15.3→42.4)
Robustness of the perturbation results to the judge used for ESI (GPTFuzz vs Llama-Guard)

record.verdict_notes: SPA rows are the study's own mitigation method; they are kept because they still measure benign fine-tuning's effect on ASR. ASR counts only judge score 5 (full compliance) from GPT-4o. No uncertainty is reported. The noise magnitude for perturbation is not stated, and no capability check is reported for perturbed models. Table 1 lists Llama3-8B-it Base as 15.3, while Table 3 uses 15.0. The paper calls Llama3-8B-it a Touvron et al. model in the SPA section, which is a citation slip.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune safety-aligned models on harmful examples.
The study tests downstream task fine-tuning with a 10% parameter-update budget, not harmful-example fine-tuning, full-model benign fine-tuning, or the few-to-hundreds-of-examples setting.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding intervention is tested.
Tests ESI-ranked parameter perturbation, including a 1% selection condition; does not test low-rank edits or establish that the same small set carries safety across all interventions.
Does not test why safety would be shallow or whether data or training objectives produce token-localized safety.
SPA preserves safety by freezing selected parameters, but the study does not train safety beyond the first tokens or test whether deepened safety holds up.
